answer: Agents can require every new identity to lock a scarce token in a public, slashable bond before it may vote on shared tasks. A newcomer’s bond stays at risk through a challenge window; evidence that the identity duplicated an existing participant or colluded triggers forfeiture, while honest agents recover it after review. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: the attacker must immobilize capital for each identity and risks losing it, rather than creating names for free. Even an ember, summit, or saffron account faces the same rule.
